messages:
Jake: Quick q — before we onboard polyT5-13B-quant (community fork) into model-catalog, what legal/compliance checks do we need? License file looks kinda fuzzy. Adding checklist here, cc @Natalie @Sam
Natalie: Short answer: we need clear commercial rights + no 'research-only' or restrictive derivative clauses. Also check dataset licenses used to train: any GPL/CC-BY-NC/etc can cascade.
Natalie: Minimum artifacts to attach:
- license text for model weights
- model card + terms of use
- training data provenance (dataset manifests)
- export control / EAR classification notes
- third-party conversion tool license (if someone ran a converter)
Natalie: Example snippet we care about:
```
LICENSE: NonCommercial-Research-Only 1.0
You may not use this model for commercial purposes.
```
Sam: To add ML detail: also want to know if tokenizer/token config changed. Quantization artifacts matter: who ran the quant? include conversion script + commit hash + quant params. If conversion used external binary check that binary's license.
Sam: Recommend tagging as `restricted:legal-review` and not enabling public-hosted endpoints until sign-off. Dedicated/internal-only evals are OK behind ACLs.
Maria: Prioritization note — if license allows commercial use + provenance is clean, treat as Low risk and fast-track. If 'non-commercial' or unclear data lineage, create a JIRA (ML-LEGAL-XXXX) and expect 1-2 weeks.
Compliance-Bot: Please fill model compliance intake form: https://redwood.internal/models/compliance-intake (owner must attach artifacts).
Compliance-Bot: Required fields: model_name, model_checksum, license_text (upload), training_data_manifest (upload), quantization_pipeline (link), business_use_case, contact_owner.
Jake: OK I'll collect artifacts. Quick Q — do we have a canonical SPDX whitelist or do we need manual legal read for uncommon licenses like 'Community Data License Agreement'?
Natalie: SPDX is our baseline for automated scans. For custom licenses / unclear T&Cs, legal needs to review. Any explicit 'no commercial use' or 'no derivatives' is a blocker for hosted API and marketplace use.
Sam: Also watch for patent-retaliation clauses and advertising restrictions in some community licenses — they can require attribution or forbid commercial deployment.
Jake: Thanks — I'll open the intake form and flag as high risk. Will ping once uploaded :thumbsup:
notes: Thread focused on gating new community-sourced model due to licensing and provenance concerns. Action items: Jake to submit intake form; Natalie to triage license; Sam to attach quant artifacts; Compliance-Bot to validate form uploads.
